stem: Which of these is **capital expenditure** for a bakery?

options.rationale: Correct: it is a non-current asset used over several years.
Materials used in production are revenue expenditure.
A running cost: revenue expenditure.
Maintenance keeps the van as it was: revenue expenditure.

explanation: Capital expenditure acquires non-current assets that benefit more than one year.

stem: Which of these is **revenue expenditure**?

options.rationale: Correct: it maintains the machine in its existing condition.
Acquiring a non-current asset is capital.
Installation is part of the cost of bringing the machine into use.
An extension improves the asset: capital.

explanation: Servicing and repairs are revenue expenditure.

stem: Legal fees paid when a business buys a shop building should be:

options.content: charged to the statement of profit or loss as revenue expenditure
options.rationale: Costs of acquiring a non-current asset are capital.

options.content: added to the cost of the building as capital expenditure
options.rationale: Correct: they are necessary to acquire the asset.
The fees are a business cost, not the owner's.

options.content: deducted from the sale proceeds of the old building
options.rationale: They are costs of buying, not selling.

explanation: The cost of a non-current asset includes the costs of bringing it into the business and into use, including legal fees.

stem: Which one of these is a **capital receipt**?

options.rationale: Rent is income from activities: a revenue receipt.
Interest is a revenue receipt.

options.content: Proceeds from selling an old delivery van
options.rationale: Correct: the sale of a non-current asset is not trading income.
Commission is a revenue receipt.

explanation: Capital receipts include loans, capital introduced and the sale of non-current assets.

stem: A clothing manufacturer's own employees build a new storeroom extension. Their wages for the work are US\$2,400. How should the wages be treated?

options.rationale: The work created an asset, so the wages are part of its cost.
The employees work for the business, not the owner personally.

options.content: As capital expenditure on the extension
options.rationale: Correct: the labour was used to create a non-current asset.
Wages are never deducted from sales.

explanation: Wages used to create a non-current asset are capitalised.
hints: Classify by what the work achieved.

stem: A machine costing US\$6,000 is wrongly debited to the repairs account. What is the effect on the financial statements of the year of purchase, ignoring depreciation?

options.content: Profit and non-current assets are both overstated by US\$6,000
options.rationale: The error is in the opposite direction.

options.content: Profit is overstated and non-current assets are understated by US\$6,000
options.rationale: An overstated expense understates profit.

options.content: Profit is understated but non-current assets are unaffected
options.rationale: The asset is missing, so non-current assets are understated.

options.content: Profit and non-current assets are both understated by US\$6,000
options.rationale: Correct: an expense has been overstated and the asset omitted.

explanation: Charging an asset as an expense reduces profit and omits the asset from the statement of financial position.
hints: What happens to expenses and to the asset?

stem: A repair costing US\$1,800 is wrongly added to the cost of equipment. What is the effect, ignoring depreciation?

options.content: Profit and non-current assets are both understated by US\$1,800
options.rationale: The error is in the opposite direction.

options.content: Profit and non-current assets are both overstated by US\$1,800
options.rationale: Correct: the expense has not been charged and the asset is too high.

options.content: Profit is understated and non-current assets are overstated
options.rationale: Not charging an expense overstates profit.
Profit is also overstated.

explanation: The repair should have been an expense. Capitalising it raises profit and asset values.

stem: A contractor's invoice of US\$7,200 for work on a factory roof is made up of US\$2,100 to replace damaged sheets and US\$5,100 to add a new skylight section. How much is capital expenditure?

options.rationale: The replacement of damaged sheets is a repair.
The repair part is revenue expenditure, not capital.

options.content: Nil, because the roof is not a new asset
options.rationale: Improvements to an existing asset are capital.
Correct: the new section is an improvement.

explanation: Mixed expenditure is apportioned: the improvement is capital; the repair is revenue.
hints: Split the invoice into repair and improvement.

stem: A bank loan received is revenue income because cash comes into the business.
explanation: False. A loan is a capital receipt and creates a liability. It is not shown in the statement of profit or loss.

stem: The cost of delivering a new machine to the factory is part of the cost of the machine.
explanation: True. Carriage on the purchase of a non-current asset is capital expenditure, because it is needed to bring the asset into use.

stem: Classify each item of Tendai's tuck shop.

left.content: Buying packets of sweets for resale
Commission received from a drinks supplier
Additional capital paid in by Tendai

explanation: The freezer and storage room are non-current assets; sweets and insurance are running costs; commission is income; the owner's capital is a capital receipt.

stem: Choose the correct words.

payload.template: Capital expenditure is recorded in the statement of {{blank:a}} and depreciated; revenue expenditure is charged to the statement of {{blank:b}}.

explanation: Capital expenditure becomes an asset; revenue expenditure is an expense of the period.

stem: Nyasha buys a milling machine for her business. She pays: price US\$9,400; delivery US\$380; installation US\$560; insurance for the first year US\$410. Calculate the cost of the machine to be capitalised.
explanation: 9,400 + 380 + 560 = 10,340. The insurance is a running cost. Including it gives 10,750.
workedSolution: 1. 9,400 + 380 + 560 = 10,340. The insurance is a running cost. Including it gives 10,750.

stem:
Chipo's payments during the year included:

| Payment | US\$ |
| --- | ---: |
| Replacement of broken windows | 640 |
| Fitting a new security gate | 1,980 |
| Fuel | 2,240 |
| Extension of the workshop | 11,800 |
| Painting the extension on completion | 870 |
| Repainting the old office | 530 |

Calculate the total revenue expenditure.
explanation: Revenue: windows 640 + fuel 2,240 + repainting the old office 530 = 3,410. The gate, the extension and the painting of the extension are capital. Counting the new painting as revenue gives 4,280.
workedSolution: 1. Revenue: windows 640 + fuel 2,240 + repainting the old office 530 = 3,410. The gate, the extension and the painting of the extension are capital. Counting the new painting as revenue gives 4,280.
hints: Painting needed to complete a new extension is part of its cost.
Replacing like with like is maintenance.

stem: Draft profit for the year was US\$28,600. A machine costing US\$6,000 had been debited to repairs. Machinery is depreciated at 10% of cost per year, straight line, with a full year's charge in the year of purchase. Calculate the corrected profit for the year.
explanation: Add back 6,000 and deduct depreciation of 10% × 6,000 = 600: 28,600 + 6,000 - 600 = 34,000. Leaving out the depreciation gives 34,600.
workedSolution: 1. Add back 6,000 and deduct depreciation of 10% × 6,000 = 600: 28,600 + 6,000 - 600 = 34,000. Leaving out the depreciation gives 34,600.
hints: Remove the repairs charge, then charge depreciation.

stem: Draft profit for the year was US\$52,000. A repair of US\$3,200 to a lathe had been added to the cost of equipment. Equipment is depreciated at 20% a year straight line, with a full year's charge in the year of purchase, and the depreciation charge of US\$640 on the repair has already been deducted in arriving at the draft profit. Calculate the corrected profit for the year.
explanation: The repair is an expense: -3,200. The depreciation of 640 charged on it was wrong, so it is added back: 52,000 - 3,200 + 640 = 49,440.
workedSolution: 1. The repair is an expense: -3,200. The depreciation of 640 charged on it was wrong, so it is added back: 52,000 - 3,200 + 640 = 49,440.
hints: Charge the repair as an expense, then remove the depreciation that was charged on it.

stem: State whether the cost of installing a new machine is capital or revenue expenditure.
explanation: Installation is a cost of bringing the machine into use, so it is capital expenditure.

stem: Distinguish between a capital receipt and a revenue receipt, giving one example of each.

points.description: Capital receipt: not from normal trading, e.g. a bank loan or the sale of a non-current asset
Revenue receipt: income from normal activities, e.g. sales or rent received

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A capital receipt is money received that is not trading income, such as a bank loan. A revenue receipt is income from normal activities, such as sales.

explanation: A definition with an example for each.

stem: Explain why wrongly treating a repair as capital expenditure overstates profit.

points.description: The repair should have been charged as an expense in the year
Capitalising it removes the expense from the statement of profit or loss, so profit is higher
Non-current assets are also overstated, and only a small depreciation charge is made against it

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: A repair is a running cost that should reduce profit in the year. If it is added to the cost of an asset, no expense is charged, so profit is overstated and the asset is shown at too high a value; only the depreciation on it is charged.

explanation: Link the classification to its effect on both statements.
hints: Which statement is affected, and in which direction?

stem: Gweru Dairy's owner proposes to treat all spending on the delivery vehicle, including fuel and servicing, as capital expenditure 'so that profit looks higher for the bank'. Evaluate this proposal.

points.description: It would overstate profit and assets by capitalising running costs
It breaches the matching and prudence concepts and could mislead the bank
Only costs that acquire or improve the vehicle may be capitalised; the rest must be charged as expenses

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The proposal would overstate profit and the value of the vehicle, because fuel and servicing are running costs that belong to the year. This ignores matching and prudence and could mislead the bank. Only the cost of acquiring or improving the vehicle may be capitalised.

explanation: A reasoned judgement using concepts and users' decisions.
hints: Which costs really create or improve the asset?

stem:
Sipho owns a printing business in Masvingo. During the year ended 31 December 2025 he made these payments:

| Payment | US\$ |
| --- | ---: |
| Purchase of a guillotine for the print shop | 8,950 |
| Transport of the guillotine to the workshop | 275 |
| Cleaning materials | 135 |
| Wiring of a new power point for the guillotine | 420 |
| Replacing a worn blade on the old press (same type) | 310 |
| Installing air conditioning in the workshop for the first time | 2,600 |

parts.label: (a)

left.content: Purchase of a guillotine for the print shop
Transport of the guillotine to the workshop
Wiring of a new power point for the guillotine
Replacing a worn blade on the old press (same type)
Installing air conditioning in the workshop for the first time

parts.explanation: The guillotine, its transport, the wiring and the new air conditioning are capital; cleaning materials and like-for-like replacement of a worn blade are revenue.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: State where the guillotine and the cleaning materials appear in Sipho's financial statements.

points.description: Guillotine: non-current asset (equipment) in the statement of financial position
Cleaning materials: an expense in the statement of profit or loss

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The guillotine is a non-current asset in the statement of financial position; the cleaning materials are an expense in the statement of profit or loss.

parts.explanation: Capital items go to the statement of financial position; revenue items to profit or loss.

explanation: This item tests classification and totals.
hints: Does the payment acquire, bring into use or improve an asset?

stem:
The draft profit for the year ended 31 December 2025 of Nyasha Transport, Harare, was US\$36,900. These errors were found:

1. A lorry costing US\$18,800 was debited to motor expenses.
2. Painting the depot walls, US\$2,150, was added to the cost of buildings.
3. Wages of US\$640 paid to employees for installing a new machine were debited to wages.

Lorries are depreciated at 25% of cost a year and machinery at 10% of cost a year, both straight line with a full year's charge in the year of purchase. No depreciation is charged on buildings. Depreciation on the machine's cost excluding installation has already been charged.

parts.label: (a)
parts.explanation: Painting maintains the walls, so it is an expense (debit) and is removed from the asset (credit Buildings).

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the depreciation on the lorry for 2025.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Calculate the corrected profit for the year.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Calculate the carrying amount of the lorry at 31 December 2025.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: The owner wishes to apply for a bank loan and will use the draft figures. Evaluate the effect of the errors on the owner's position.

points.description: Profit was understated by 12,526 (corrected 49,426 against draft 36,900)
Non-current assets were understated, so the bank sees a weaker asset base
The errors are not all in the same direction (the painting was overstated as an asset), so the correction must be made item by item
The corrected figures give a fairer picture and should be used in the application

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The draft profit of US\$36,900 was understated by US\$12,526 and the lorry was missing from non-current assets, so the business looked weaker than it is. The painting was wrongly treated as an asset, so some figures were overstated. The corrected figures give a true picture and should be used for the loan application.

parts.explanation: Use figures from the correction and refer to the user's decision.

explanation: This item tests correcting misclassification and its effect on profit and assets.
hints: Capital items charged as expenses raise profit when corrected; capitalised expenses lower it.
